title: Decode streams weights; prefill batches rows
why: Shows the memory-bound decode dataflow and the batched prefill path with the 16-row packing and measured throughput scaling.
nodes: Decode: 1 row per stream, packed up to 16 (ROUND_ROWS=16)
notes: Unified memory (111.5 GB) feeds the memory bus (273 GB/s) into the SM; each layer's weight matrix is streamed and multiplied by an activation vector. The KV cache stores key/value vectors per layer per past token, read during decode and appended one token at a time. Prefill processes many prompt tokens at once (39,237 tok/s over 98 sampled requests). Decode processes one token per stream per step, with the kernel packing up to 16 rows per weight load (ROUND_ROWS=16). Measured throughput: 59.1 tok/s single-stream vs 106.2 tok/s aggregate at four concurrent streams (1.80x). SM clock is 2,197 MHz observed against a 3,003 MHz silicon ceiling. | Left-to-right flow: prompt enters both drafter and target; drafter emits k candidate tokens; target consumes prompt plus all k candidates in one pass. Label the verification pass as a batched GEMM with k-row activation matrix: weight traffic same as one-token decode, arithmetic grows roughly k, attention and KV writes grow by k. Annotate the context-attention term using the chapter's mean prompt length 130,659 tokens and example k=4. Optionally show a cost bar comparing one decode step vs k=4 verification: one weight stream plus four rows of attention over 130,659 keys per layer plus four KV writes. Do not invent per-kernel timings; the chapter only gives aggregate prefill 3.33 s, decode 8.38 s, TTFT 3.46 s over 98 requests. | Flow is left to right: q samples x; p supplies the ratio; the accept test splits into accept or reject. For the numeric example, x=A has accept probability min(1,0.2/0.5)=0.4; reject residual is (0,0.2,0.1) with Z=0.3, normalized to (0,2/3,1/3). Labelled outputs: A=0.2, B=0.5, C=0.3. The diagram should label accepted mass min(q,p), residual mass max(0,p-q), and the final sum to p. | Flow is left to right. Labels on the flow: k draft tokens, acceptance probability α, draft time per token t_d, verification time for k tokens t_v, baseline target decode time per token t_t. Expected output tokens per round E = (1 - α^{k+1}) / (1 - α); round time = k t_d + t_v; speedup = E t_t / (k t_d + t_v). Prose examples: k=4, α=0.7, t_d=0.2 t_t, t_v=1.0 t_t gives E=2.7731, round time 1.8 t_t, speedup 1.54; α=0.3, t_d=0.05 t_t gives E=1.4251, round time 1.2 t_t, speedup 1.19; t_v=1.2 t_t, α=0.1 gives E=1.1111, round time 1.24 t_t, speedup 0.896. | Draw the draft tree with prompt as root and A,B,C,D as four draft positions. Beside each draft position show its attention-mask row over the four draft positions; every row also attends the prompt. Annotate that A's KV entry is shared by the B and C branches. After verification, mark prompt, A, and B as kept and C and D as freed. No axes; the labelled quantities are the four draft positions and the mask bits given in the chapter. | Arrows: h_t feeds all three heads; head 1 predicts t+1 from h_t; head 2 predicts t+2 from h_t plus embedding of t+1; head 3 predicts t+3 from h_t plus embeddings of t+1 and t+2. The heads share the embedding and output head. Training adds cross-entropy at offsets 1, 2, and 3 to the main next-token loss. At inference the heads produce a draft chain that the target verifies. Label the operational acceptance rate 67.6% as 42,181 accepted tokens out of 62,390 drafted from /metrics, aggregated over mixed traffic, and the 1.80x concurrency ratio as the other bounding number.
